meta.subtitle: Hollowgate → Dunmore · Vanya's thread · Eric Huwithakay · The Gilded Veil

sections.title: Core Truth — What This Arc Is
sections.subtitle: Not a personal arc · Evidence that persists · The gap nobody has filled

content.text: What This Arc Is (GM Only)

Vanya was given her first true contract: a gate scribe in Hollowgate had begun noticing inconsistencies in convoy records — questions that were becoming dangerous. She was to secure any relevant records or notes he carried, then remove him. Cleanly. Quietly. Without drawing attention to the work.

She arrived and found him already dead in the kobold tunnels. Someone else got there first. The contract's outcome is technically complete — the scribe is silenced — but she did not do it, does not know who did, and is now holding her target's satchel.
The party does not know this. When Vanya takes the satchel, it reads as recovering evidence. Keep the player's knowledge distinct from the party's.

Inside the satchel: records, maps, a final note. And tucked into the inner fold, a personal notation pointing to Dunmore — a location called The Briar Cup, a recognition phrase, and the instruction to 'tell her.' Vanya was not given this phrase. She found it on the man she was sent to kill.

The Gilded Veil's contract was to silence Eric and recover his intel. The note in his satchel points to Dunmore — a location, a recognition phrase, someone waiting. The Veil doesn't know this exists. Following it is Vanya's own call, because it's how you actually find out what he knew and who else knew it.

The woman at The Briar Cup will believe Eric sent Vanya. He did not. Vanya found the phrase on her target's body. That gap is the tension of the scene — not a test anyone designed, just the consequence of Vanya doing the job properly.
Relationships & Stakes

PC. Her first true contract: silence a gate scribe asking inconvenient questions. Arrive, recover his records, remove him. She arrived and found him already dead. She took the satchel anyway — that was the job. The note inside it pointed to Dunmore. The recognition phrase written there was not given to her by anyone. She found it on her target.

Gilded Veil asset, Tallow Street apothecary. Eric's Dunmore contact. She was receiving his information about altered manifests and waiting for his confirmation to pass it up the chain. When Vanya arrives with the correct phrase, Ilyra knows Eric is dead without being told.

Vanya's handler. Operates from The Rusty Bin salvage yard. Methodical, unreadable. Receives the manifests. Asks three questions. Does not mourn Eric. Does not need to — she processes what was lost and adjusts.

Intelligence network, primarily operating in a neighboring country. Fringe Fastingbreak presence. Has no knowledge of the Concord's existence. The Concord is aware of the Veil and tolerates it. The two organizations have never intersected directly — until, perhaps, now.

sections.title: Part One — The Abandoned Well
sections.subtitle: Hollowgate · Occurs during the Missing Convoys escape sequence

content.text: The kobold tunnels are mostly dark and mostly quiet by the time the party reaches the far end. The well shaft appears between two collapsed support beams — not a cave feature, a structure. Old. Not kobold work. Something heavy has been dropped into it recently.
The Body
Male, mid-forties. Well-dressed for tunnel work — he planned to be here, had been here before. Satchel still strapped across his chest. He was pushed in. The fall didn't kill him.
Wound below the sternum. Thin, precise, upward angle — not a kobold spear, not a claw. A blade. Handled by someone who knew where to put it.

He was stabbed before the kobolds reached him, or after they passed, or someone came through the tunnels behind him. Establish the impossibility gently — let the party feel the gap before they can articulate it.

content.label: Medicine DC 12
content.reveal: The wound angle is consistent with a right-handed attacker facing him — stabbed from the front. He saw it coming or turned toward it. The blade was thinner than a shortsword. This was deliberate.

content.text: The Satchel

items: A bronze signet stamp — Sarynthian design. Most party members won't recognize it immediately. Aurelia will.
A partial tunnel map, hand-drawn — more detailed than Krobb's. He had been here before.
A note in tight, careful handwriting: 'Kobolds. Someone is paying them.' That is all he had time to write.

content.text: Tucked inside the inner fold of the satchel — smaller, folded twice, separate from the other documents. Easy to miss if you're not looking. Not addressed to anyone. Two sentences only.
DM. The Briar Cup. Tell her the western road remained dry.

For Vanya: 'DM' is Eric's personal shorthand for Dunmore — his notation system for his own notes. 'Tell her' is the instruction. The western road remained dry is the recognition phrase for Ilyra Marr at The Briar Cup in Dunmore.

'DM' is Eric's notation for Dunmore — his shorthand, for his own notes. The Briar Cup is somewhere in Dunmore. 'Tell her the western road remained dry' is a recognition phrase, pointed at a woman who was waiting for him to arrive. He didn't arrive. He won't.
Vanya was sent to make sure he never arrived anywhere again. The note is addressed to no one. It was never meant for her. She's going to use it anyway.

Ilyra Marr will believe Eric sent Vanya. He did not. Vanya will walk into that meeting carrying credentials she took from her target's body. The GM should hold this tension carefully — Ilyra trusts the protocol. The protocol has been compromised in a way neither of them can see.
Tallow Street is not dramatic. A chandler, a dry goods counter, a narrow apothecary with no signage that you could easily walk past twice. Vanya doesn't walk past it.
Finding It
Modest. No signage. Herbs in the window — dried, labeled with small cards in careful handwriting. The kind of shop that serves people who already know it's there.
Ilyra Marr works the counter. She is not visibly nervous. She is not visibly anything. She is waiting.
Back storeroom. Shelving, sacks, the smell of dried sage and old wood. A narrow stair, unlit, going down. A heavy door at the bottom with an iron handle shaped like a vine.
The Briar Cup: three tables, four oil lamps, no windows. It smells of herbs from above and old stone from below. Whatever conversations have happened here stayed here.
The space should feel contained, not threatening. Ilyra chose it because it has no sightlines to the street and the ambient noise from the apothecary above masks sound. It is professionally selected.
The Meeting
Vanya says: "The western road remained dry."
Ilyra sets down what she was holding. "Then you came in from the east."

The protocol is satisfied. Ilyra has never met Eric in person — dead-drop only. She knows his handwriting. She does not know his face, his voice, or his sex. The phrase is the only verification she has, and it worked.

This opens a genuine player choice. Vanya can present as a contact Eric sent — straightforward, lower risk. Or she can attempt to present as Eric directly. Difficult: Ilyra may ask questions only Eric would know, and Vanya's knowledge comes only from his satchel. But Ilyra has no face to check the claim against. If Vanya goes this route, let Ilyra's questions come naturally from the conversation — don't announce the skill check. Let the player feel the tightrope.

What she asks depends on how Vanya presents. If Vanya implies Eric sent her: "He usually comes himself when he can. What kept him?" If Vanya attempts to present as Eric: "You're not what I expected from your handwriting." — said neutrally, curious rather than suspicious. She has never seen Eric. She has no face to compare. She is reading the situation, not yet alarmed.
Either path converges: Ilyra needs to know what she's working with before she passes anything on. She is reading Vanya the entire time and will not announce that she's doing it.

If Eric's death surfaces — volunteered or pressed — Ilyra goes quiet. "How." Told about the wound, below the sternum, not kobold weapons: "That means it wasn't them." She does not explain who 'them' is. She moves on. She does not know what Vanya was contracted to do. She may never find out. The information she's about to hand over was meant for Eric — it's going to the party through the person who was sent to remove him.
The Manifests

Eric was tracking unusual tariffs and altered shipping records. Ilyra is the one who sourced the data — she can read manifests by instinct, trained by years of watching what gets declared and what doesn't.

items: Specific cargo rerouted through Dunmore's secondary customs gate during shift transitions — three times in six months.
Each time: cargo with no legitimate destination. Offloaded to an unmarked warehouse on the east dock. Never claimed.
Two manifests have been altered: cargo reclassified mid-route, customs stamps mismatched with the issuing gate's records, destination field overwritten.

content.text: What She Passes On
She was waiting for Eric's confirmation before passing the manifests up the chain. He never sent it.
She has copies of two manifests. She will pass them to Vanya instead. "Someone has to carry this forward. That's you now."

Two documents on thin paper, clearly copied in Ilyra's handwriting from originals. Fields of note: cargo type (reclassified from 'dry goods' to 'equipment parts'), origin gate (primary) vs. routing gate (secondary), destination left blank, two different customs stamps from the same checkpoint.

The manifests are evidence, not a puzzle to solve immediately. The party may not understand their significance for several sessions. That is correct. Ilyra doesn't fully understand them either — she knows they're wrong. What they point to is Seren Vale's question to answer.

sections.title: Part Three — The Rusty Bin
sections.subtitle: Dunmore · Eastern edge · Salvage yard with a back room

content.text: The Rusty Bin is easy to find if you know what you're looking for — a working salvage yard on the eastern edge of the city, wagon parts and scrap iron stacked against the fence. There's a gate in the east wall and a back room that isn't on any signage.
The Space

Mismatched furniture. A table being used as a bar — bottles, no labels on some of them. Four or five people at various tables who are never quite the same people twice. The ambient noise from the yard — metal on metal, rolling wheels, shouted transactions — fills the room well enough to mask anything said below a shout.
Seren Vale sits at the same table every time. She does not greet. She waits.
Not warm. Not cold. Precise. She runs the salvage yard legitimately — the records are clean, the employees are real, the business turns a small profit. Everything else runs through the back room.
She will not ask Vanya how she is. She will not make small talk. She will ask three questions.
The Debrief — Three Questions
She means: what information came out of Hollowgate. Not Eric's death — what he had, what the party recovered, what Ilyra passed on. Vanya reports. Seren listens without interrupting.
She means: who in the party understands the significance of what they're carrying. She is doing threat assessment. Her expression does not change regardless of the answer.
She means Eric. Not the person — the operational capacity. What intelligence died with him. What the chain no longer has access to.
She does not ask how he died unless Vanya raises it. She is not sentimental about assets. She adjusts.
What Seren Shares

After examining the manifest copies: "The Veil wanted Eric's information because the pattern isn't local. Someone is using Dunmore's logistics infrastructure for something. We don't know who. The Concord doesn't appear to know either — and they watch this city."
She does not elaborate. She does not need to. The party now knows there is something happening in Dunmore that two separate intelligence networks have noticed and neither can identify.
This is the hook forward. Do not resolve it here. The manifests are evidence. The unmarked warehouse is a location that exists. Seren knows where it is. She does not share that yet.
How It Ends
Seren slides a folded note across the table. Not money — a contact protocol. A location in Dunmore, a time of day, a phrase to use if Vanya needs to reach her. Standard Veil procedure.
"You've been useful. Payment is standard." She stands, which means the meeting is over.
"We'll be in touch."
Not a threat. Not a promise. Simply true. She operates in Dunmore. The party will be in Dunmore. She will hear what they do.

The Rusty Bin stays in the world. This is not a one-time location. If the party does something visible in Dunmore — solves the propaganda investigation, confronts the monstrosity — Seren Vale notices. The Veil notices. That is the texture of a world with moving parts.

conclusion.title: GM Summary — Running This Arc
items: This arc is not a dungeon. It is not a mystery with a clean resolution. Run it like a briefing that opens more questions than it closes.

The abandoned well discovery happens inside the Missing Convoys escape beat — no separate scene needed. The satchel search is the moment. Let Vanya's player decide how much to share with the party in real time.
Ilyra Marr is not hostile. She is cautious and then practical. The recognition phrase is ritual — let it land before she speaks. Her 'he's dead, isn't he' should feel inevitable, not dramatic.
Seren Vale's three questions are the whole debrief. Do not add warmth or humor. She is thorough and efficient. The manifests going 'up the chain' is final — the party doesn't follow them from here.

The payload of this arc is one sentence from Seren: 'The Concord doesn't appear to know either.' The party now knows there is a layer of activity in Dunmore that both the Concord and the Gilded Veil are blind to. That is the hook forward.

The Rusty Bin is a recurring location. The Gilded Veil is a recurring presence. The contact protocol Seren hands over is a real door — Vanya can use it later. Let the party know this matters without telling them why yet.
